messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service=kv-store (prod-west) severity=critical. Trigger: post-deploy canary v2.14.0 — rapid 5xx spike and p95 latency > 1200ms. Canary nodes: pool-canary-3, pool-canary-4. Logs show repeated KV timeout errors.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty PD-8821 created and escalated to schedule 'infra-oncall'. Initial urgency: high. Notify: @infra-oncall, @sre-oncall. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-8821

Maria G: Ack. Oncall Maria here. Jumping in. 

Sahil K: on it — checking dashboards (latency, error-rate, request distribution). Looks like canary only but p95 for production path is creeping up. Might be cache evictions.

Alex T: I saw similar on staging yesterday with a kernel regression in the runtime. Can we confirm model size/quant config changed in this deploy?

Joanne R: FYI release notes: v2.14.0 enabled aggressive KV-prefetch + new memory allocator flags. Rollout target: 10% canary.

Maria G: Running quick queries:
```
curl -sS https://metrics.redwood/api/query?metric=kv_time+p95 | jq .value
# returns 1.26s
kubectl get pods -n kv-prod -l role=canary -o wide
```

Sahil K: logs from pool-canary-4: repeated `ERR kv_timeout` and `mem_alloc_fail` around same timestamps as errors. Attaching snippet: `2026-02-15T03:12:12Z ERROR kv: timeout id=...`

oncall-sre: Reassigning PD incident to Maria G (ack). Sending notify to release-owner @Alex T and eng-runtime.

Maria G: Decision call: isolate canary group, stop traffic to pool-canary-3/4 and shift to baseline. Plan: 1) Pause rollout, 2) Drain canary pods, 3) Fallback to previous revision on canary nodes, 4) Monitor for error rate drop. Anyone object?

Luke S: +1 for pause and drain. If allocator flag is the culprit we should revert config on canaries first to avoid full rollback.

Alex T: I can revert allocator flag remotely on the canary nodes. If that doesn't help, we'll rollback the canary image to v2.13.7.

Maria G: Executing drain now — command: `kubectl cordon pool-canary-3 && kubectl drain pool-canary-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

Joanne R: Noted customer impact: a subset of requests (10% rollouts) saw increased error rate and latency. No broad outage yet, but some higher-tier customers reported transient failures via support channel ticket #SUP-3242.

Sahil K: Error rate falling after drain started — p95 down to ~450ms, 5xx count decreasing. Metrics: `5xx_last_5m: 120 -> 18`.

pagerduty-bot: PD-8821 status updated: acknowledged by Maria G. Incident responder: infra-oncall.

Maria G: Rolling back the canary image to v2.13.7 on pool-canary-4 as a test: `kubectl set image deployment/kv-service kv=redwood/kv:2.13.7 -n kv-prod --record`

Alex T: Reverted allocator flag on canary nodes as well (toggle `--mem-alloc=legacy`). Watching for memory errors.

Sahil K: Good sign — mem_alloc_fail logs dropped. p95 now ~220ms. Continuing to observe for 5m.

Joanne R: I'm drafting a short customer-facing note for affected customers and support. Will post in #customer-impact once we confirm stabilization.

Maria G: After 8 minutes, metrics look stable and errors are within baseline. Propose closing PD-8821 as mitigated and mark root cause as allocator flag + config interaction introduced in v2.14.0. Open follow-up: runtime team to run canary config tests.

Luke S: Recommend postmortem: include perf regression test for allocator changes + gating in canary rollout pipeline. +1 for follow-up ticket.

Maria G: PD-8821 -> status: resolved (mitigated). Creating follow-up MTL ticket and assigning to eng-runtime and release-owner. Thx team. :thumbsup: 

pagerduty-bot: PD-8821 closed by Maria G. Incident timeline will be auto-generated.

incident-bot: Note: Handoff complete. If any new alerts spike please reopen or file PD-8821 follow-up.
